title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover race condition
author: Priya Raman
body: Motivation: a production incident (SUP-9832) exposed a rare race in the SLO enforcer's regional failover path that caused duplicate failover attempts and transient routing flaps when a region briefly reported degraded SLOs while a concurrent backoff timer was expiring. This led to increased request latency and a small spike in error budgets for a subset of customers. Goal: provide a minimal, safe hotfix that removes the race and adds extra guards so the enforcer does not trigger duplicate failover actions under contention. Root cause: the enforcer's state machine allowed 'failover_requested' to be set from two concurrent code paths (threshold breach and manual toggle) without atomic coordination; a subsequent retry loop could schedule multiple failovers because the in-memory coordinator didn't dedupe attempts before dispatching region-change events. Summary of changes: - Add an atomic compare-and-set for failover_requested in the coordinator (coordinator.go) to ensure one in-progress failover at a time. - Introduce a short hysteresis window (200ms) to coalesce near-simultaneous requests originating from different sources. - Move failover dispatch into a single worker goroutine per customer to provide ordered, single-threaded execution and easier tracing. - Add metrics and tags to track coalesced vs explicit failover triggers (slo.enforcer.failover_coalesced, slo.enforcer.failover_trigger). - Tighten unit tests and add a deterministic concurrency test that simulates overlapping threshold and manual triggers. - Add an integration smoke test for regional failover ordering under artificial latency. Compatibility and scope: this is a narrow hotfix targeting the enforcer module used in Dedicated and Private control plane deployments. No API changes. No config schema changes. Rollout plan: 1) Canary deploy to staging and one low-traffic dedicated cluster (canary window 1 hour) 2) Monitor slo.enforcer.* metrics and canary error budget for 2 hours 3) Gradual rollout to remaining Dedicated pools over 6 hours if metrics stable 4) Immediate rollback plan: set environment flag SLO_ENFORCER_FAILOPEN=true to disable automated failovers and rely on manual ops. Testing: added unit tests for compare-and-set and coalescing logic. Integration test added to perf-canary harness to run a synthetic burst test. Local CI: all unit/integration tests pass; one flaky end-to-end test was quarantined and tracked in ENG-4290. Related: references Linear ENG-4287 and incident SUP-9832.
commits: cf3a1d7: enforcer: atomically set failover_requested flag and add coalescing
9b2f7e4: enforcer: single-worker dispatch and ordering guarantees
a7e5b2c: tests: deterministic concurrency test and integration smoke test
d1f0c3a: metrics: add failover_trigger / failover_coalesced counters
review_comments: Ethan Cole: please add a small benchmark for the added worker goroutine to show no regression under 1k rps - answered: added micro-benchmark and results in coordinator_test.go (no measurable regression).
Marta Liu: small nit: extract 200ms hysteresis to a constant and document rationale - answered: moved to const and added comment with reasoning and link to ENG-4287.

Diego Ramos: can we avoid creating per-customer goroutines at scale? ensure we reuse a worker pool - replied: design keeps one lightweight goroutine per active customer (customers with no activity are cleaned up after 5m); follow-up ticket ENG-4302 created to iterate on a shared pool implementation.
Marta Liu (approve): LGTM after tests and metrics added. Ethan Cole (approve). Diego Ramos (request changes -> resolved).
release_notes: Hotfix: fixes race in SLO enforcer regional failover that could cause duplicate failovers and transient routing flaps. Adds coalescing, ordering guarantees, and observability metrics.
